4. ā (आ)   (as a prefix to verbs, especially of motion, and their derivatives) near, near to, towards (see ā-√ kram (आ-√ क्रम्) &c.; in the Veda (Vएद), of course, the prefix is separable from the verb; in a few cases, RV. i, 10, 11 and v, 64, 5, a verb in the imperative is to be supplied; with roots like gam (गम्), yā (या), and i (इ), ‘to go’, and 1. dā (दा), ‘to give’, it reverses the action; e.g. ā-gacchati (आ-गच्छति), ‘he comes’; ā-datte (आ-दत्ते), ‘he takes’). (As a prep. with a preceding acc.) near to, towards, to, RV. (with a preceding noun in the acc., as joṣám (जोषम्) or varám (वरम्)) for, RV. (with a following acc.) up to … exclusively, AitBr. (with a preceding abl.) from, RV.; AV. out of, from among (e.g. bahubhyá ā (बहुभ्य आ), ‘from among many’), RV. towards (only in asmad ā́ (अस्मद् आ), ‘towards us’), RV. (with a following abl. cf. Pāṇ. ii, 1, 13 & 3, 10) up to, to, as far as, RV.; AV. &c. from, RV. i, 30, 21 (with a preceding loc.) in, at, on RV.; AV. (As an adv. after words expressing a number or degree) fully, really, indeed (e.g. trir ā́ divas (त्रिर् आ॑ दिवस्), ‘quite or fully three times a day’; mahimā vā́m indrā (महिमा वाम् इ॑न्द्रा)gnI pa/nizWa A/,, ‘your greatness, O īndra (ईन्द्र) and āgni (आग्नि), is most praiseworthy indeed’, &c.), RV. (after a subst. or adj.) ‘as, like’, (or it simply strengthens the sense of the preceding word), RV., (after a verb), RV. v, 7, 7; KenaUp. (as a conjunctive particle) moreover, further, and (it is placed either between the two words connected [rarely after the second, RV. x, 16, 11, or after both, RV. x, 92, 8] or, if there are more, after the last [RV. iv, 57, 1 and x, 75, 5]; see also ā (आ)taS ca s.v.) In classical Sanskṛt it may denote the limit ‘to’, ‘until’, ‘as far as’, ‘from’, either not including the object named or including it (sometimes with acc. or abl. or forming an adv.) e.g. ā-maraṇam (आ-मरणम्) or ā-maraṇāt (आ-मरणात्), ‘till death’, Pañcat. gloss_eng: also, on the other hand, in turn, on the contrary
master_entry_str: 3. u (उ)   ind. an enclitic copula used frequently in the Veda (Vएद)s; (as a particle implying restriction and antithesis, generally after pronominals, prepositions, particles, and before nu (नु) and su (सु), equivalent to) and, also, further; on the other hand (especially in connexion with a relative, e.g. ya u (य उ), he on the contrary who &c.) This particle may serve to give emphasis, like id (इद्) and eva (एव), especially after prepositions or demonstrative pronouns, in conjunction with nu (नु), vai (वै), hi (हि), cid (चिद्), &c. (e.g. ayam ú vām purutamo (अयम् उ वा॑म् पुरुतमो) … johavīti (जोहवीति) [RV. iii, 62, 2], this very person [your worshipper] invokes you &c.) It is especially used in the figure of speech called Anaphora, and particularly when the pronouns are repeated (e.g. tam ú stuṣa indram tam gṛṇīṣe (तम् उ स्तु॑ष इन्द्रम् तम् गृणीषे) [RV. ii, 20, 4], him I praise, īndra (ईन्द्र), him I sing). It may be used in drawing a conclusion, like the English ‘now’ (e.g. tad ú tathā na kuryāt (तद् उ तथा॑ न कुर्यात्) [ŚBr. v, 2, 2, 3], that now he should not do in such a manner), and is frequently found in interrogative sentences (e.g. ka ú tac ciketa (क उ तच् चि॑केत) [RV. i, 164, 48], who, I ask, should know that?) phāṇini (फ्āṇइनि) calls this particle uñ (उञ्) to distinguish it from the interrogative u (उ). In the phada-pāṭha (फद-प्āṭह) it is written ūm (ऊम्). In the classical language u (उ) occurs only after atha (अथ), na (न), and kim (किम्), with a slight modification of the sense, and often only as an expletive (see kim (किम्)); u (उ) — u (उ) or u (उ) — uta (उत), on the one hand — on the other hand; partly — partly; as well — as.

gloss_eng: on the one hand - on the other hand, now - now, both - and; and, also
master_entry_str: 2. uta (उत)   ind. and, also, even, or, RV.; AV.; ŚBr.; ChUp. &c. often used for the sake of emphasis, especially at the end of a line after iti (इति) or a verb (e.g. sarva-bhūtāni tam pārtha sadā paribhavanty uta (सर्व-भूतानि तम् पार्थ सदा परिभवन्त्य् उत), all creatures, O king, certainly always despise him, MBh. iii, 1026), MBh.; Bhag. &c. (As an interrogative particle, generally at the beginning of the second or following part of a double interrogation) or, utrum-an (e.g. katham nirṇīyate kiṃ syān niṣkāraṇo bandhur uta viśvāsa-ghātakaḥ (कथम् निर्णीयते किं स्यान् निष्कारणो बन्धुर् उत विश्वास-घातकः), how can it be decided whether he be a friend without a motive or a violator of confidence? Hit.), Kum.; Kathās.; Bhartṛ.; Sāh. &c. in this sense it may be strengthened by āho (आहो) (e.g. kaccit tvam asi mānuṣī utā (कच्चित् त्वम् असि मानुषी उता)ho surANganA, art thou a mortal woman or divine? ṅala (ङल)), or by āho-svit (आहो-स्वित्) (e.g. śālihotraḥ kiṃ nu syād utā (शालिहोत्रः किं नु स्याद् उता)hosvid rAjA nalaH, can it be Śālihotra (Śāलिहोत्र) or king ṅala (ङल)?) Rarely kim (किम्) is repeated before uta (उत) used in this sense (e.g. kim nu svargāt prāptā tasyā rūpeṇa kimutā (किम् नु स्वर्गात् प्राप्ता तस्या रूपेण किमुता)nyAgatA, has she arrived from heaven or has another come in her form? Mṛcch.), Amar.; MBh. &c. (As a particle of wishing, especially at the beginning of a sentence followed by a potential) would that! utinam! (e.g. utā (उता)DIyIta, would that he would read!) 3. vi (वि)   ind. (prob. for an original dvi (द्वि), meaning ‘in two parts’; and opp. to sam (सम्), q.v.) apart, asunder, in different directions, to and fro, about, away, away from, off, without, RV. &c. &c. In RV. it appears also as a prep. with acc. denoting ‘through’ or ‘between’ (with ellipse of the verb, e.g. i, 181, 5; x, 86, 20 &c.) It is esp. used as a prefix to verbs or nouns and other parts of speech derived from verbs, to express ‘division’, ‘distinction’, ‘distribution’, ‘arrangement’, ‘order’, ‘opposition’, or ‘deliberation’ (cf. vi-√ bhid (वि-√ भिद्), -śiṣ (-शिष्), -dhā (-धा), -rudh (-रुध्), -car (-चर्), with their nominal derivatives) sometimes it gives a meaning opposite to the idea contained in the simple root (e.g. √ krī (क्री), ‘to buy’; vi-√ krī (वि-√ क्री), ‘to sell’), or it intensifies that idea (e.g. √ hiṃs (हिंस्), ‘to injure’; vi-√ hiṃs (वि-√ हिंस्), ‘to injure severely’).
